title: Multi-Scale Detection of Anomalous Spatio-Temporal Trajectories in Evolving Trajectory Datasets

problem.claim: Detecting anomalous trajectories online as new trajectories continuously enter a dataset is important but challenging.

gap.claim: Existing solutions determine anomalies from trajectory shapes or routes while ignoring anomalies caused by differing sampling rates or time offsets.

contributions.claim: A multi-scale model, MST-OATD, is proposed for anomalous streaming trajectory detection using both spatial and temporal trajectory aspects.
The model extracts trajectory features at multiple scales.
A learned ranking model updates the training set as new trajectories arrive to support model evolvability and changing trajectory patterns.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real datasets report that the model outperforms state-of-the-art solutions.
The model is reported to support real-time anomaly detection.
The learned ranking model delivers promising results when newly arrived trajectories are used to refresh the training set.

narrative_sequence.summary: Trajectories represent timestamped object movement and encode spatial and temporal mobility patterns.
The dataset evolves through continuous inclusion of new trajectories, creating a need for online anomaly detection.
Existing methods focus on shapes or routes and omit sampling-rate and time-offset anomalies.
MST-OATD uses multi-scale spatial and temporal modeling, with learned ranking to update training data as trajectories arrive.
Experiments on real datasets report competitive performance, real-time detection, and promising training-set updates.

source_observation.claim: Anomaly detection for evolving trajectory data should account for both spatial and temporal aspects, including multiple feature scales.

interpretation.claim: A detector limited to geometric route or shape similarity may miss anomalies introduced by temporal sampling differences or offsets.

application.claim: For streaming mobility data, combine multi-scale spatial-temporal representation with online anomaly scoring.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that multi-scale modeling is necessary or effective across domains beyond the reported trajectory setting.

source_observation.claim: A learned ranking model updates the training set as new trajectories arrive to address changing trajectory patterns.

interpretation.claim: Continual training-data maintenance may help an anomaly detector adapt to evolving streams.

application.claim: Use an update mechanism that ranks newly arrived examples when maintaining training data for streaming detection.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the update frequency, ranking criteria, or risks of incorporating newly arrived trajectories.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, evaluation metrics, dataset names, or baseline details.
The abstract does not define the anomaly types, multi-scale architecture, ranking objective, or training-set update protocol.
The abstract does not report computational constraints or latency measurements supporting real-time detection.
